newsitem.title: USA: Nortel in data/voice integration plan.
newsitem.headline: Nortel in data/voice integration plan.

text.p: Northern Telecom Ltd unveiled Wednesday a new generation of integrated networks that can handle data, voice, video and other content, applying phone network expertise to corporate information networks.
The Toronto-based company said it is launching capital Power Networks, a system designed to give users of complex corporate networks access to a host of multimedia features.

Nortel also announced a new set of strategic partner and customer ties built around the new Power Networks platform, including close links to Cabletron Systems Inc, a supplier of local area networking equipment.

"In our increasingly digital global economy, the network is the business. Traditional networks are struggling to keep up with this new paradigm, and a performance gap between business demands and the ability of networks to meet them has emerged," said Rick Faletti, president of enterprise networks at Nortel.
He said that with the launch of Power Networks, Nortel hoped to bridge that gap.

All Power Networks incorporated managed personal networking, which let users tap the network using personalized multimedia appliations, flexible network access, switched network infrastructure and virtual private networking, the company said.
A Power Network reduced network complexity and management requirements and lowered annual operating costs, it said.
They were custom-designed to individual competitive needs and emphasized the use of routing capability coupled with switching technology, Nortel said.
By integrating legacy networks on asynchronous transfer mode or frame relay backbones, Power Networks also provided bandwidth access, it said.
Cabletron said it was allied with Nortel in implementing Power Networks.
Cabletron was providing LAN technology to Power Networks, but also implementing a Power Networks switch in its own corporate network, the company said.
Richardson, Texas,-based Enterprise Networks is a division of Nortel, which provides communications equipment, services and network solutions.
